topicName: Advanced Scheduling, Taints, Tolerations, and Affinity
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced Scheduling, Taints, Tolerations, and Affinity in Kubernetes"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kubernetes provides robust mechanisms to control how pods are placed onto specific nodes within a cluster. While basic scheduling relies on resource requests and limits, advanced scheduling leverages taints, tolerations, and node affinity to enforce strict workload isolation and preferential placement."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Taints and Tolerations"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Taints allow a node to repel a set of pods. Tolerations are applied to pods, allowing (but not requiring) them to schedule onto nodes with matching taints. Together, they ensure that pods are not deployed on inappropriate nodes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"NoSchedule: If the taint is not tolerated, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PreferNoSchedule: The scheduler will try to avoid placing the pod, but it is not mandatory."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"NoExecute: If the taint is added to an existing node, non-matching pods are evicted immediately."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"kubectl taint nodes worker-1 dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To allow a pod to land on the tainted node, define a toleration in the pod specification:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: cuda-app
    image: nvidia/cuda:latest
  tolerations:
  - key: "dedicated"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "gpu"
    effect: "NoSchedule""},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Node Affinity and Anti-Affinity"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"While taints repel pods, node affinity attracts them. Node affinity is conceptually similar to nodeSelector, allowing you to constrain which nodes your pod can be scheduled on based on node labels."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: Hard rule. The scheduler cannot place the pod unless the rule is met."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: Soft rule. The scheduler will try to enforce preferences, but will fallback if unavailable."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: affinity-pod
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
            operator: In
            values:
            - antarctica-east-1
            - antarctica-west-1
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Inter-Pod Affinity and Anti-Affinity"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Inter-pod affinity and anti-affinity allow you to constrain which nodes your pods can be scheduled on based on the labels of pods already running on those nodes. This is extremely useful for keeping related services close together (latency reduction) or spreading replicas across failure domains (high availability)."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redis-cache
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: store
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: store
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - labelSelector:
              matchExpressions:
              - key: app
                operator: In
                values:
                - store
            topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
      containers:
      - name: redis
        image: redis:alpine"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining taints, tolerations, and advanced affinity rules, you can design highly resilient, secure, and performant Kubernetes architectures tailored to complex enterprise requirements."}]
